title: ALMA observation of the disruption of molecular gas in M87
question: Is there molecular gas (CO 2-1) in the M87 filament southeast of the nucleus, and how does it relate to the AGN radio lobe and shock?

what.value: Shock pressure map and Mach number >=1.2 from Chandra

evidence.quote: report the presence of a shock with a Mach number of at least 1.2, driven by the expansion of the 6 cm radio lobe

what.value: CO(2-1) to CO(1-0) flux density ratio of 3.2

evidence.quote: a CO(2–1) to CO(1–0) flux density ratio of 3.2 (cite: david2014)
the \[O iii\]/H$\beta$ emission line ratios reported by (cite: werner2013) show a strong decrease with radius

recipe.goal: Reduce data and image CO(2-1) cube
recipe.method: CASA reduction, uvcontsub, Briggs imaging, primary beam correction
3D mask in position-velocity space on 10 km/s binned cube, keeping >3 sigma detections
Mass formula from CO(2-1) integral with Galactic XCO and CO(2-1)/(1-0) ratio
assumptions: XCO = 2e20 cm^-2/(K km/s); ratio 3.2; D_L = 16.1 Mpc; z=0.00436

recipe.goal: Compare CO and Halpha inside vs outside radio lobe
recipe.method: Two 9x9" regions; HST F660N Halpha fluxes; CO 3 sigma upper limit inside

evidence.quote: The total flux measured in the CO(2–1) line is $(5.5 \pm 0.6) \times 10^{-18}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$
$S_{\rm CO}\Delta\nu = 0.56 \pm 0.06$ Jy km s$^{-1}$ is the emission integral
a narrow line width, $\sigma=27\pm3$ km s$^{-1}$

answer_key.quantity: CO(2-1) 3 sigma upper limit, inner region

evidence.quote: the $3\sigma$ upper limit on the CO(2–1) flux from the inner region is $1.3\times10^{-18}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$
$(3.1\pm0.3) \times10^{-14}$ and $(2.5\pm0.2) \times 10^{-14}$ erg s$^{-1}$ cm$^{-2}$ nearer and further from the AGN, respectively

we estimate that in this scenario 1.1 Myr have elapsed between the shock passage and the observed destruction of the molecular gas
